title: The last graded piece of a collapsed finite filtration
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], $V$ an object, and $n\ge0$ an integer. Let $F$ be a decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration] on $V$ with $F^0V=V$, $F^{n+1}V=0$, and $\operatorname{gr}^p_FV=F^pV/F^{p+1}V=0$ for every integer $0\le p<n$. Then $F^pV=V$ as subobjects for all $0\le p\le n$, the inclusion $j:F^nV\to V$ is an isomorphism, and the canonical quotient $\rho:F^nV\to\operatorname{gr}^n_FV$ is an isomorphism. More precisely, for any objects $A,B$ of $\mathcal A$ and isomorphisms $a:A\to B$ and $c:\operatorname{gr}^n_FV\to B$, there is a unique map $f:A\to F^nV$ with $\rho\circ f=c^{-1}\circ a$; it is $f=\rho^{-1}\circ c^{-1}\circ a$. The map $j\circ f:A\to V$ is an isomorphism with inverse $a^{-1}\circ c\circ\rho\circ j^{-1}$. If $V$ is a zero object, then $A$ is a zero object. These conclusions include $n=0$, when the range $0\le p<n$ is empty.

proof.text: For each integer $0\le p<n$, let $u_p:F^{p+1}V\to F^pV$ be the inclusion. By [def-sp-filtration] its cokernel is $\operatorname{gr}^p_FV=0$, so [lem-weil-pbc-preadditive-epi-iff-cokernel-zero] makes $u_p$ an epimorphism. It is also a monomorphism. Here is the inverse argument directly from [def-sp-abelian]: write $u_p$ as a kernel of some $t:F^pV\to T$. Since $tu_p=0$ and $u_p$ is epi, $t=0$. The kernel universal property applied to $\mathrm{id}_{F^pV}$ gives $r_p:F^pV\to F^{p+1}V$ with $u_pr_p=\mathrm{id}$. Monicity of $u_p$ then gives $r_pu_p=\mathrm{id}$. Thus $u_p$ is an isomorphism over $V$ and $F^{p+1}V=F^pV$ as subobjects.

proof.text: Induct on the nonnegative integer $k\le n$ with claim $F^kV=V$ as subobjects. The base case is the hypothesis $F^0V=V$. If $k<n$, Step 1 gives $F^{k+1}V=F^kV$, proving the successor case. This proves every asserted equality, including for integer indices $0\le p\le n$. Equality with the full subobject means that the representing inclusion $j:F^nV\to V$ is isomorphic over $V$ to $\mathrm{id}_V$, hence has an inverse. Concretely the isomorphism over $V$ supplies $s:V\to F^nV$ with $js=\mathrm{id}_V$, and monicity gives $sj=\mathrm{id}_{F^nV}$.

proof.text: By [def-sp-filtration], $\rho:F^nV\to\operatorname{gr}^n_FV$ is a cokernel of the inclusion $F^{n+1}V\to F^nV$. The inclusion's source $F^{n+1}V$ is zero by hypothesis, so that inclusion is the zero morphism. The cokernel universal property applied to $\mathrm{id}_{F^nV}$ gives $s:\operatorname{gr}^n_FV\to F^nV$ with $s\rho=\mathrm{id}_{F^nV}$. Both $\rho s$ and the identity on $\operatorname{gr}^n_FV$ have composite $\rho$ with the cokernel projection, so uniqueness in the same universal property gives $\rho s=\mathrm{id}$. Thus $\rho$ is an isomorphism with inverse $s$.

proof.text: Define $f=\rho^{-1}c^{-1}a$. Associativity and $\rho\rho^{-1}=\mathrm{id}$ give $\rho f=c^{-1}a$. If $f_1$ also satisfies the equation, composing on the left by $\rho^{-1}$ gives $f_1=\rho^{-1}c^{-1}a=f$. Put $g=a^{-1}c\rho j^{-1}:V\to A$. Cancellation of adjacent inverse pairs gives $(jf)g=j\rho^{-1}c^{-1}aa^{-1}c\rho j^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_V$ and $g(jf)=a^{-1}c\rho j^{-1}j\rho^{-1}c^{-1}a=\mathrm{id}_A$. Thus $jf$ is an isomorphism with exactly the inverse claimed. If $V$ is a zero object then $\mathrm{id}_V=0$, and $\mathrm{id}_A=g\mathrm{id}_V(jf)=0$; consequently every map from or to $A$ is zero (compose with $\mathrm{id}_A$), so $A$ is a zero object. For $n=0$, Step 1 has no indices, Step 2 uses only its base case, and Steps 3 and 4 apply with $F^1V=0$.
